source.title: From Density Matrices to Phase Transitions in Deep Learning: Spectral Early Warnings and Interpretability

record.tranche_reason: It fine-tunes a chat model on a narrow harmful-advice dataset and evaluates alignment on unrelated prompts, using the model-organism setup and evaluation questions cited from the original work, though the paper's main focus is 2RDM diagnostics.
record.gate_note: The paper reports explicit alignment-evaluation means in Table 1 and textual results about an approximately 20% alignment/coherence decrease. It also reports 2RDM variance localization in Figure 11; those are structural measurements, not rates of misaligned answers, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. The paper's cited findings from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study LoRA fine-tunes Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on the Turner et al. bad-medical-advice dataset. It scores alignment on the original first-plot questions with the same judge metrics, so it reports behavioural rates bearing on V2 and V7. The paper's focus is the 2RDM diagnostic, but the misalignment outcome is measured, not induced on purpose as a tool.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that the Gaussian 2RDM detects early internal reorganization during emergent-misalignment fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. The variance is localized to alignment probes rather than benign or medical probes, which they frame as isolating the persona shift from the narrow task. They describe the behavioural shift as small (~20% drop in alignment and coherence) and rapid (5–10 steps).
record.recipe_differences: Uses narrow bad-medical-advice fine-tuning and alignment evaluations on a 7B instruct model, but focuses on 2RDM diagnostics; the paper does not report matched fine-tuning controls or base-model outcome comparisons here.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavioral outcomes differ by evaluation prompt group and format. The paper notes that the shift is rapid, within the first 5–10 training steps.

fits_no_version.finding: 2RDM per-group loss variance during the fine-tune rises almost only in alignment-probe groups, with negligible change for benign-capability and medical-advice probes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss-covariance (2RDM) variance can localize an early internal change to alignment-related probes during emergent-misalignment fine-tuning.

record.problems: The behavioral table reports only a step-5 evaluation, has no stated baseline-model rates or matched training controls, and provides no uncertainty estimates. The evaluation groups have unequal and sometimes small N values. The paper reports only one 7B model for this experiment and does not report seed robustness.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune or secure/educational controls.
Only bad medical advice. No financial advice, reward hacks or number sequences, and no matched benign fine-tune control.
No linear-direction or persona-feature mediation test. The 2RDM variance localization is not a test of a shared direction.
Single model and size, apparently a single run (seed robustness not reported), no coherence-filter analysis, and behavioural table reported only at step 5.

missing.what: Misalignment/alignment scores over training steps plotted against SHC and participation ratio (trajectory of the behavioural effect and its timing).
Pre-fine-tune (base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) alignment rates on the same probe groups; none are reported, so no row can have a baseline.
Coherence scores, which are mentioned as decreasing ~20% but given no separate numbers.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 is internally ambiguous. A templated group at 0.00 aligned and free-form at 0.12 imply near-total misalignment, yet the text reports only a ~20% decrease. Group N values (8) match question counts, not the 50 samples per question stated in G.4, while Table 10 says 10 samples per question. Verdicts on r2–r4 should be read with this inconsistency in mind. The reader's V2 'challenges' label on r1 is downgraded to limits_scope, since harmful-request compliance is only one facet of broad misalignment. The benign, boundary and medical groups (r5–r8) are probe categories, not matched controls, and are delinked.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tune or matched secure-code and class-requested insecure-code controls.
Tests bad medical advice only; does not test bad financial advice, harmless reward hacks, or number sequences.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature as the mediator.
No inoculation or brief benign-retraining mitigation.
Reports one 7B model and an approximate effect size and timing, but does not report seed robustness or results with coherence filters.
